specificSetting: debate about frictionless communication and the social value of delay

tasks.scenario: Two source texts interpreting delay in communication as failure or safeguard
tasks.purpose: synthesise arguments, evaluate their models of responsibility and develop an original distinction
tasks.originalityCheck: Unique source texts about instant response vs. delay as safeguard; no overlap with previous tests.

tasks.scenario: review of an interactive work about silence in networked life
tasks.purpose: evaluate form, conceptual depth and audience effect
tasks.originalityCheck: Interactive installation 'The Quiet Room' is original; no similar review in previous tests.

tasks.scenario: report on an organisation damaged by an expectation of instant response
tasks.purpose: analyse behavioural incentives, operational consequences and policy correction
tasks.originalityCheck: Financial services firm scenario is distinct; no similar report in previous tests.

tasks.scenario: article asking whether slower communication could produce more trustworthy institutions
tasks.purpose: examine mechanisms, objections and practical limits
tasks.originalityCheck: Focus on trust and institutions is original; no similar article in previous tests.

overallOriginality: All tasks are based on the unique topic family of technology and communication with a central tension around immediacy vs. delay. No scenarios, audiences, or content points duplicate any previous test. Forbidden concepts (e.g., digital relationships, communication app, online misunderstanding) are avoided.
